newsitem.title: USA: Rate drop seen triggering heavy corp debt issuance.
newsitem.headline: Rate drop seen triggering heavy corp debt issuance.

text.p: Another busy day is expected for the corporate bond primary sector as lower interest rates prompt U.S. corporations to capitalize on cheaper financing and issue debt now, dealers said.

"With the (Treasury) market trading up 3/4 of a point we should see another busy day," said one high-grade syndicate source. "We'll probably see some names that were lingering in the market start to come."
AT 1013 EDT/1413 GMT, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 27/32 at 98-2/32 to yield 6.78 percent, compared to Wednesday's close at 6.84 percent.
One such corporate deal is Hartford Life's $700 million three-part debt offering, rumored to be coming to market for several weeks now, players said.

The deal is expected to include a seven-year issue, with price talk seen at 50 basis point over Treasuries, a 10-year issue, with spread talk seen at 62.5 basis points, and a 30-year issue, seen pricing at a spread of 80 basis points, dealers said.
Earlier, Treasury prices rose sharply after the Commerce Department reported a 0.1 percent drop in May U.S. retail sales, contrary to expectations for a 0.4 percent rise.
Commerce also revised the decline in April retail sales to 0.9 percent, three times the size of a 0.3 percent drop originally reported.
Excluding auto sales, retail sales slipped 0.1 percent in May, versus expectations for a 0.3 percent rise.
After Wednesday's $4.0 billion in new straight corporate debt issuance, more offerings are seen on the way, dealers said.
So far today, Public Service Electric & Gas has issued $235 million in first and refunding mortgage bonds due 2000 at 28 basis points over Treasuries.
Another $250 million in a par preferred deal is expected to come from Argentaria Capital Ltd, syndicate players said.
Dealers said a majority of issues priced recently have done very well, holding their spread or tightening a few basis points when freed to trade in the secondary market.
"Potash's 10-year paper tightened three to four basis points in the after market," said one syndicate source. "The issue came at 67 basis points over but later was quoted at 63."
On Wednesday Potash Corp sold $400 million in 7.125 percent 10-year notes via Smith Barney.
Mercantile Bancorp's three issues, also priced on Wednesday, were seen trading at firm levels.
"Mercantile Bancorp's four-year, seven's and ten's freed up and are holding their (spread) levels," said one player.
With steady demand by investors for corporate paper, supply should continue to pour in, players said.
"Investor appetite for corporate paper continues to be strong ... the demand is still very much there," said one player.
Another $1.35 billion in new high-yield corporate debt is expected by the end of the week, dealers said.
Axteca Holdings is expected to bring $255 million in five-year 144A notes. Price talk is seen at 175 to 200 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Chase Telecommunications is expected to bring $125 million in seven-year 144A notes via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
Di Giorgio Corp is slated to bring $140 million in 10-year 144A senior notes via Merrill Lynch. Price talk is seen between 10.0 and 10.25 percent, players said.
((--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675))
